elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XXII is replaced with "Licensor shall have no right of first refusal and no right to match any third-party offer to purchase the assets of, or to merge or consolidate with, the Licensee." The disclosure/notice trigger, the five-business-day Exercise Period and the tail sentence permitting consummation only after Licensor declines are all struck, so no matching or best-offer obligation on Licensee survives. The rendered negation covers both limbs of the original (asset purchase and merger/consolidation), and no other cited fee provision (Article V tiers, Supplemental Payments, rebate shares) imposes a best-price undertaking on Licensee.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; its condition does not apply because after the edit there is no Customer MFN/right-to-match obligation at all — Article XXII now expressly negates any Licensor right of first refusal or right to match. With no surviving obligation, there is nothing requiring a product limitation.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; the original duration hook ("During the term of this Agreement") is deleted along with the operative right, so no Customer-side MFN runs for any period. A duration cap is moot where the obligation is eliminated entirely.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Conditional element; no comparison mechanic remains to be carved out — the requirement to give notice of a bona fide third-party offer and to afford Licensor the same terms has been removed in full.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the operative text eliminates the right-to-match/most-favoured-offer mechanic burdening Licensee and states affirmatively that Licensor has no right of first refusal and no right to match, leaving no residual notice, waiting-period or same-terms obligation.

Correct rule allocation: a disclosure plus right-to-match mechanic in Vendor's favour is properly treated under MFN rather than exclusivity, and the edit does not touch the Article XX change-of-control consent or Article XXIV(c) assignment consent, so the same commercial term is not redlined twice.

Minimal: the change is confined to Article XXII (heading conformed to "NO RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL"); no affirmative transfer permission, notice waiver, survival tail, expense allocation or other extra requirement is added, and no favourable Customer-side language elsewhere is removed. The concise negation replaces the deleted mechanic without adding operative obligations.

Preserves intent: the deleted defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" were self-contained within Article XXII and are not relied on elsewhere in the cited text, so no dangling cross-reference or undefined term results; the tail sentence permitting consummation after a declined exercise is correctly removed because it is meaningless once the right is negated.

Minor drafting note (not a defect): the negation refers to "the assets" rather than the original "all or substantially all of the assets"; because this is a negation of a Vendor right, the broader formulation operates in Customer's favour and does not create an obligation.
